desc: Run exhaustive minimax on small states to discover the N-even winning condition.
Implement component traversal to compute component sizes, bipartition class sizes, edge counts, and missing-edge parity/zero status.
Implement the N-odd branch: output Aoki iff M is odd.
Test the current program on the three public samples.
Extend targeted abstract minimax to larger families and collect counterexamples.
Derive the correct even-N rule: K odd components, K=2 always winning, K>=4 depends on M parity, K=0 depends on M parity XOR parity of even components with both bipartition sides odd.
Implement the proven even-N rule as an O(N) solver and remove research/exact-minimax fallbacks.
Test on edge cases: N=1, N=2, empty graph, terminal complete bipartite graphs, K=0/2/>=4, even components with both sides odd, and large sparse graphs.
Finalize the program to read stdin and print exactly Aoki or Takahashi.
